description:
The gate status arms label every failure `GATE_CHECK_ERROR`, print a bare `null` for gates never run, and reach storage to detect transposed arguments. This moves them to library handlers.

## Background

`GateCommands::Status` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` (latest run, `--all` run history, flat and findings views) builds `GateRunHistoryResponse` and related responses inline and reports any failure under `--json` as `GATE_CHECK_ERROR` (exit 3) at four sites while the human path uses the classifier. Its "not run" branches print `JsonOutput::<Option<()>>::success(None)`, so stdout is the bare text `null`. Its transposed-argument guard calls `executor.storage().resolve_issue_id` twice, then prints an inline `INVALID_ARGUMENT` `JsonError` or calls `exit(2)` on the human path. `GateCommands::StatusAll` prints a success envelope and then exits 4 when not all gates passed, so its exit code matches no envelope code. `gate status` falls back to `CommandResponse` in the schema.

A handler in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/` takes its parsed arguments and a `CommandContext` (the executor and the `OutputMode { json, quiet }`) and returns `anyhow::Result<Outcome<R>>`; one registration per group generates the group's dispatch and its schema response lookup. Success responses are types defined in the output module (`crates/jit/src/output/`) or output constructors wrapping a command-layer result, each deriving `JsonSchema` and a human rendering; list payloads are `ListEnvelope<K, T, E>` instantiations; failures are returned as errors that `jit::output::failure::classify` maps to one code and exit status; a non-zero findings result is `Outcome`'s findings variant, rendered under `--json` as the failure envelope with the report in `error.details` and its registered code as the exit status.

On main, `run()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` parses the arguments and calls `dispatch()` in `main.rs`, which holds the command match; the arms and inline code this issue places in `run()` live in `dispatch()`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `run()` dispatches `gate status` (all views, including `--all` history) and `gate status-all` to handlers in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/gate.rs`, and `main.rs` keeps no arm body for them.
- [hard] REQ-02: The transposed-argument guard uses an executor predicate instead of `storage().resolve_issue_id` and raises a typed error classified as `INVALID_ARGUMENT` with exit 2 on both paths.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each view returns a registered typed response, the not-run case is a typed object instead of bare `null`, human output uses the shared gate-run-status renderer, and the schema names the response; a test states the not-run payload.
- [hard] REQ-04: `gate status-all` with a failed or unrun gate returns a findings outcome, and a test asserts the failure envelope with `GATE_FAILED`, exit 4 and the report in `error.details`; failures carry the classifier's code instead of `GATE_CHECK_ERROR`, which a test asserts for one non-missing-gate failure.
- [hard] REQ-05: Where a leaf's exit codes change, its rows in `CommandSchema::generate_command_exit_codes` (`crates/jit/src/schema.rs`) state the new codes and `docs/reference/exit-codes.md` is regenerated.
- [hard] REQ-06: Human output, success payloads and exit codes of these leaves are otherwise unchanged, and the existing suites pass without weakened assertions.

## Notes

8673dc5e changes how manual attestation appears in gate status.

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`; inventories with function and arm citations: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md`.
title: Gate status commands move to library handlers
